sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Backend services overview (Cloud Load Balancing)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17 (English page of the Google Cloud documentation mirror). Relevant text: the capacity scaler 'provides a way to scale the target capacity manually'; 0 means the backend is 'completely drained', 0.1 to 1.0 set the share of capacity in use; 0 cannot be used when the backend service has only one backend. That a drained backend stops getting new requests while in-flight ones finish, and the error budget arithmetic, are from memory of the connection draining and SRE pages (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the SRE on call at Larkin Grocers. The storefront runs behind a global external Application Load Balancer with two managed instance group backends, us-east1 and us-west1, each sized to carry all traffic alone. At 11:50 a regional configuration push broke us-east1: 40% of its responses are 503. The 30-day availability SLO (99.9%) has 18 minutes of budget left, and the lunch peak starts at 12:30.
handover: us-west1 runs the previous configuration and is healthy at 35% utilization.
The configuration push is being investigated by the platform team; a fix is not yet known.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the global load balancer, its two regional backends and where requests go.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: what failed, how you mitigated without losing the region, and how it returns.

parts.label: Failed
parts.modelAnswer: Since the 11:50 push, us-east1 returned 40% 503s; us-west1 was clean at 35% utilization and can autoscale to carry all traffic.

parts.label: Mitigated
parts.modelAnswer: Drained web-us-east1 with capacity scaler 0; us-west1 scaled to 22 instances and the burn rate fell to 0.3x. Deleting the group would have removed redundancy and evidence; restarting brought back the same configuration.

parts.label: Return
parts.modelAnswer: us-east1 returns 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 once its fix is verified, and a per-backend 5xx alert catches one bad backend early.

expertPath.text: 5xx only in us-east1; us-west1 can scale to 30; both backends at 1.0; 18 min of budget.
Capacity scaler 0 on us-east1; stepped return plan and alert.

regionDeleted.headline: Drain, don't destroy
regionDeleted.body: A capacity scaler of 0 takes a backend out of rotation and keeps it for diagnosis and a gradual return. Deletion turns an incident into a rebuild.

sloBreached.headline: Mitigate first, debug second
sloBreached.body: When one backend is bad and another can carry the load, redirect traffic away at once, then find the cause.

drained.headline: Good: redirect traffic, keep the evidence
drained.body: You read errors by backend, checked the healthy region could carry everything, drained the bad one with the capacity scaler, watched the burn rate fall, and planned a stepped return with alerting.

scoring.modelReasoning: All the errors come from us-east1, and us-west1 can grow to carry all traffic. Drain us-east1 with a capacity scaler of 0: new requests go to us-west1, in-flight ones finish, and the broken backends stay for debugging. Watch the burn rate fall, then return the region in steps once fixed. Deleting the group loses redundancy and evidence; restarting reapplies the same bad configuration.
